chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim and Ya`qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Fuddal, from Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (AS)
In His Word, the Mighty and High: (the nature made by Allah is which He has made men). He (AS) said: He created them with Divine Unity.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic term 'Fitrah' refer to according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies the 'Fitrah' mentioned in Surah Ar-Rum as the innate recognition of Tawhid, establishing monotheism as the primordial state of human nature. This interpretation underscores the Shia belief that belief in One God is not merely a learned doctrine but an intrinsic, uncorrupted disposition embedded in every human soul from creation.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 4. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan alSaffar said, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Hashim; and Ya`qub ibn Yazid, on the authority of Ibn Fuddal, on the authority of Bukayr, on the authority of Zurarah that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS)
was asked to interpret the Word of the Mighty and High: The nature made by Allah is which He has made men. He (AS) said: “He created them with Divine Unity.”
